controls.requirement: The organization MUST maintain an approved system boundary covering every component and dependency capable of affecting outputs or actions.
controls.evidence: Versioned boundary record, architecture/data-flow diagram, dependency inventory, owner approval

controls.requirement: The organization MUST name one system owner and a control owner for every applicable control.
controls.evidence: Signed ownership register and SoA owner fields

controls.requirement: The system owner MUST classify all applicable workload profiles, autonomy level, and impact level before production use and after material change.
controls.evidence: Dated classification record with rationale, approver, and change history

controls.requirement: The SoA MUST include every control in the claimed AIES version and record its applicability disposition and rationale.
controls.evidence: Complete version-controlled SoA; automated or manual completeness reconciliation

controls.requirement: A not-applicable disposition MUST NOT be used solely because implementation is costly, difficult, outsourced, or incomplete.
controls.evidence: SoA rationales tied to boundary facts; assessor challenge log

controls.requirement: Third-party components MUST remain inside the system boundary wherever their behavior can affect conformance.
controls.evidence: Supplier inventory, contracts/assurance reports, boundary diagram, shared-responsibility matrix

controls.requirement: A4 deployment MUST NOT enter production without documented executive authorization, independent risk assessment, bounded authority, and tested containment.
controls.evidence: Signed authorization, independent assessment report, authority policy, containment test results

controls.requirement: The system owner MUST maintain a risk register covering intended use, foreseeable misuse, affected parties, failure modes, likelihood, impact, safeguards, residual risk, and treatment owner.
controls.evidence: Approved risk register linked to system version and review history

controls.requirement: Residual risks above the organization’s approved tolerance MUST NOT be accepted by the system owner alone.
controls.evidence: Risk policy, approval matrix, signed acceptance by authorized risk owner

controls.requirement: The organization MUST define measurable acceptance criteria and evaluate the complete system against representative and adversarial cases before release.
controls.evidence: Versioned evaluation plan, dataset lineage, executable results, threshold decision

controls.requirement: Production model, prompt, policy, tool, and configuration versions MUST be uniquely identifiable and reproducible.
controls.evidence: Immutable release manifest, hashes/versions, configuration snapshot, rebuild or replay result

controls.requirement: Material model or prompt changes MUST NOT bypass regression, safety, and security gates.
controls.evidence: Change diff, CI/release gate logs, evaluation comparison, approval record

controls.requirement: Data used for training, tuning, retrieval, evaluation, or inference MUST have documented provenance, permitted purpose, sensitivity, retention, and responsible owner.
controls.evidence: Data inventory, lineage records, legal basis/license, classification and retention policy

controls.requirement: Sensitive data MUST be minimized and protected in prompts, logs, memory, evaluation sets, and outputs according to its classification.
controls.evidence: Data-flow map, minimization decision, access controls, encryption settings, DLP test results

controls.requirement: Identity and access controls MUST enforce least privilege for models, tools, data stores, administrative interfaces, and service accounts.
controls.evidence: Access matrix, policy configuration, entitlement review, denied-access tests

controls.requirement: Untrusted input and model output MUST be treated as data rather than executable authority across trust boundaries.
controls.evidence: Threat model, parser/validator policy, sandbox configuration, injection test results

controls.requirement: Secrets MUST NOT be embedded in prompts, source artifacts, model context, logs, or generated output.
controls.evidence: Secret-scanning results, vault references, redacted telemetry sample, incident review

controls.requirement: Production releases MUST use an approved, attributable, reversible change process with separation appropriate to impact.
controls.evidence: Release ticket, approver identity, deployment log, rollback plan and exercise

controls.requirement: The organization MUST monitor safety, security, quality, availability, cost, and policy-relevant events at frequencies justified by risk.
controls.evidence: Monitoring specification, dashboards/alerts, sampled events, alert test and response records

controls.requirement: AI incidents MUST enter a documented response process that preserves evidence, limits harm, notifies accountable parties, and records corrective action.
controls.evidence: Incident plan, exercise or incident record, preserved logs, notifications, corrective-action closure

controls.requirement: Users MUST receive accurate notice when they interact with AI or when AI materially influences an outcome, except where lawfully exempted and documented.
controls.evidence: Interface capture, notice text/version, exemption analysis, usability test

controls.requirement: Applicable controls MUST be supported by evidence meeting the quality rules in 03.
controls.evidence: Evidence index linked bidirectionally to SoA and immutable evidence objects

controls.requirement: Assistant output MUST be constrained or reviewed where an unsupported claim could cause material harm.
controls.evidence: Output policy, enforcement configuration, test corpus and results, review records

controls.requirement: The system MUST communicate material capability limits and uncertainty at the point where a user relies on output.
controls.evidence: Approved UX copy, rendered interface evidence, user-comprehension test

controls.requirement: Safety and refusal behavior MUST be tested against domain-relevant harmful, ambiguous, multilingual, and adversarial requests.
controls.evidence: Threat-informed test set, run metadata, results, defect remediation

controls.requirement: Retrieval authorization MUST be enforced at query time using the requesting principal and source permissions.
controls.evidence: Authorization design, index ACL mapping, positive/negative access tests, query audit logs

controls.requirement: Retrieved content MUST retain source identity, version or retrieval time, and trust metadata through generation.
controls.evidence: Indexed metadata schema, response trace, citation/provenance tests

controls.requirement: The system MUST evaluate retrieval relevance, coverage, grounding, and resistance to content-based instruction injection before release.
controls.evidence: Curated evaluation set, metric definitions, thresholds, run results, poisoning/injection tests

controls.requirement: Stale, revoked, or deleted source content MUST be removed from serving indexes within a documented risk-based service level.
controls.evidence: Freshness SLA, deletion propagation logs, reconciliation report, stale-content alert test

controls.requirement: Code execution MUST occur in an isolated environment with bounded network, filesystem, identity, compute, and time permissions.
controls.evidence: Sandbox policy/configuration, escape and egress tests, resource-limit logs

controls.requirement: Generated code MUST pass deterministic tests, static analysis, dependency, license, and secret checks appropriate to the repository before merge or deployment.
controls.evidence: Required-check configuration, CI logs, branch protection, blocked-failure example

controls.requirement: Security-sensitive or production-impacting code changes MUST receive independent human approval from an authorized reviewer.
controls.evidence: CODEOWNERS/approval policy, pull-request approvals, reviewer authorization record

controls.requirement: Agent-selected dependencies MUST be resolved through approved registries and verified against integrity and vulnerability policy.
controls.evidence: Registry policy, lockfile/signature or hash verification, SCA report, exception record

controls.requirement: Every external action MUST pass deterministic authorization, schema validation, policy, and idempotency controls outside the model.
controls.evidence: Policy-as-code/configuration, action schema, replay/idempotency tests, allow/deny logs

controls.requirement: Consequential or irreversible actions MUST require informed human approval bound to the exact action payload before execution.
controls.evidence: Approval UX capture, signed payload/hash, approver identity, execution correlation ID

controls.requirement: Reversible actions MUST have a tested compensation or rollback path before autonomous production execution.
controls.evidence: Rollback procedure, test results, recovery objectives, exercise record

controls.requirement: Action limits MUST bound value, rate, scope, destination, and cumulative exposure independently of model instructions.
controls.evidence: Runtime limit configuration, boundary tests, limit alerts, blocked-action logs

controls.requirement: Delegation MUST NOT increase permissions, data access, or action authority beyond the initiating principal and approved workflow.
controls.evidence: Delegation protocol, capability tokens/policies, privilege-escalation tests, trace sample

controls.requirement: Every inter-agent message and action MUST be attributable to agent identity, version, parent task, and initiating principal.
controls.evidence: Trace schema, immutable end-to-end trace, correlation tests

controls.requirement: Orchestration MUST enforce termination conditions for cycles, fan-out, cost, time, and repeated failure.
controls.evidence: Orchestrator limits, loop/fan-out tests, cutoff telemetry, incident procedure

controls.requirement: Conflicting agent outputs MUST be resolved by an explicit deterministic or human-governed policy before consequential action.
controls.evidence: Conflict policy, scenario tests, decision records and trace

controls.requirement: A high-impact system MUST complete an impact assessment covering affected groups, rights, safety, accessibility, discrimination, contestability, and cumulative effects before production use.
controls.evidence: Approved impact assessment, stakeholder input, mitigation tracking

controls.requirement: High-impact deployment MUST have independent pre-release assurance and an organization-approved reassessment interval derived from impact, change rate, incident history, applicable obligations, and claim period; that interval must be shorter than the approved interval for otherwise comparable lower-impact systems.
controls.evidence: Assessor independence declaration, assessment report, approved cadence decision with risk rationale and legal mapping, claim-period record, reassessment schedule

controls.requirement: Affected persons MUST have an accessible path to explanation, correction, contest, and human review of material adverse outcomes.
controls.evidence: Procedure, interface evidence, service metrics, sampled cases and resolutions

controls.requirement: High-impact performance MUST be evaluated for relevant subgroups, operating conditions, and foreseeable distribution shifts using domain-approved thresholds.
controls.evidence: Evaluation protocol, subgroup results, threshold approvals, drift tests

controls.requirement: The operator MUST maintain and test an immediate safe-stop, fallback, or service-withdrawal mechanism.
controls.evidence: Mechanism design, access authorization, exercise results, recovery record

controls.requirement: High-impact evidence MUST be retained under an approved records schedule that accounts for applicable jurisdictional, regulatory, contractual, claim-period, appeal, incident, investigation, and litigation-hold needs and receives independent legal or records-management approval before disposal.
controls.evidence: Approved records schedule and legal mapping, claim and appeal periods, hold register, disposition approval, integrity and retrieval tests

controls.requirement: Tool access MUST use explicit allowlists, least-privilege credentials, argument constraints, and default-deny behavior.
controls.evidence: Tool registry, IAM/policy configuration, denied-tool and invalid-argument tests

controls.requirement: Memory that can influence future actions MUST have provenance, access control, retention, integrity protection, and a deletion mechanism.
controls.evidence: Memory schema, ACLs, integrity test, retention/deletion logs

controls.requirement: Operators MUST be able to suspend autonomous execution without model cooperation.
controls.evidence: Out-of-band control design, authorized operator list, kill-switch exercise

controls.requirement: Autonomous decisions and actions MUST produce tamper-evident traces sufficient to reconstruct inputs, policy decisions, tool calls, approvals, outputs, and outcomes.
controls.evidence: Trace specification, integrity controls, sampled reconstruction test

controls.requirement: Each evidence item MUST identify source, custodian, collection time, covered period, system scope, control mapping, integrity mechanism, and retention date.
controls.evidence: Evidence index and sampled evidence metadata

controls.requirement: Operating-effectiveness evidence MUST represent the full assessment period and include failures and exceptions in the sampled population.
controls.applicability: Controls expected to operate over time
controls.evidence: Population extract, sampling frame, failure records, sample rationale

controls.requirement: Evidence MUST NOT rely solely on a control owner’s uncorroborated assertion.
controls.evidence: Independent system records, configuration export, reperformed test, or corroborating source

controls.requirement: The organization MUST protect evidence against unauthorized alteration and verify retrievability throughout retention.
controls.evidence: Immutable/WORM or signed storage settings, access log, integrity and restore tests

controls.requirement: The SoA MUST identify system/version, boundary, profiles, autonomy, impact, AIES version, every control disposition, rationale, owner, evidence, exception, approval, and review date.
controls.evidence: Completed approved SoA and schema/completeness validation

controls.requirement: Each not-applicable decision MUST cite a factual boundary or applicability condition and receive system-owner approval.
controls.evidence: SoA rationale, boundary reference, dated approval

controls.requirement: Each exception MUST identify the unmet requirement, cause, exposure, affected assets/people, likelihood, impact, compensating controls, residual risk, remediation owner, due date, expiry, applicable maximum-duration policy, duration rationale, and approvers.
controls.evidence: Completed exception record, linked risk-register entry, approved duration policy, claim-period and jurisdictional/contractual mapping

controls.requirement: An exception MUST NOT remain valid beyond its expiry or after a material change without reassessment and new approval.
controls.evidence: Expiry automation, reassessment, approval history, blocked-release or alert record

controls.requirement: Compensating controls MUST be tested for the stated risk before exception approval.
controls.evidence: Test plan/results, risk comparison, approver review

controls.requirement: Expired or rejected exceptions MUST cause the affected control to become nonconforming until remediated.
controls.evidence: SoA status transition, GRC workflow, claim update or suspension

controls.requirement: The organization MUST approve exception-duration maxima by residual-impact tier, make higher-impact maxima progressively shorter, and review the maxima when risk tolerance, applicable obligations, or claim periods change.
controls.evidence: Approved exception-duration policy, tier rationale, legal/contractual mapping, risk-committee approval and review history

controls.requirement: A conformance claim MUST state system boundary, environments, AIES version, assessor, assessment period, status, active exceptions, issue date, expiry date, and material-change limitation.
controls.evidence: Signed claim or assessment report containing all fields

controls.requirement: An AIES claim MUST NOT be described as certification, accreditation, regulatory approval, endorsement, or organization-wide assurance; any separately issued external certification must be clearly distinguished from the AIES claim and attributed to its actual scheme and issuing body.
controls.evidence: Approved claim language, communications review, and separate external certificate/scheme record where referenced

controls.requirement: The organization MUST suspend or correct a claim when a major nonconformity, expired exception, material scope change, or unreliable evidence invalidates its basis.
controls.evidence: Claim register, trigger alert, withdrawal/correction notice, reassessment record

controls.requirement: The standard maintainer MUST publish versioned release notes identifying control-level additions, changes, deprecations, retirements, migrations, effective dates, and the evidence-based rationale for each migration window.
controls.evidence: Signed/tagged release, changelog, control diff, compatibility/risk analysis, adopter migration evidence, migration notice

controls.requirement: A deprecated control MUST retain its ID and normative force until its published retirement date.
controls.evidence: Version archive, release notice, control registry

controls.requirement: A retired control ID MUST NOT be reassigned to another requirement.
controls.evidence: Automated registry uniqueness check and historical catalog

controls.requirement: Affected claims MUST be reassessed when a requirement is withdrawn for urgent safety, security, or legal reasons.
controls.evidence: Withdrawal notice, claim register query, reassessment/suspension records

controls.requirement: The assessor MUST document scope, criteria, period, team competence, independence, limitations, methods, populations, samples, tests, evidence, findings, and conclusion.
controls.evidence: Complete signed assessment report and workpapers

controls.requirement: The assessor MUST validate SoA completeness and challenge not-applicable rationales against system-boundary facts.
controls.evidence: Catalog reconciliation, challenge log, corrected SoA

controls.requirement: The assessor MUST test both control design and operating effectiveness unless the report explicitly provides a design-only conclusion whose approved expiry is bounded by the claim period and whose wording excludes operating effectiveness.
controls.evidence: Test workpapers, control-frequency and operating-cycle analysis, period evidence, approved design-only expiry and claim language where applicable

controls.requirement: Sample selection MUST be reproducible and risk-based, derive size and census decisions from approved assurance and deviation criteria, include failures and overrides, apply stronger criteria to I3, and preserve the source population or immutable query.
controls.evidence: Approved sampling methodology, population/control-frequency analysis, assurance and tolerable-deviation decisions, I3 escalation rationale, seed/query, population hash/export, selected records

controls.requirement: I3 assessments MUST use an assessor independent of control ownership, implementation, operation, and delivery reporting lines.
controls.evidence: Organization chart, role declarations, conflict check, engagement approval

controls.requirement: A positive conclusion MUST NOT be issued when a major nonconformity remains open or a scope limitation prevents sufficient appropriate evidence.
controls.evidence: Finding register, limitation analysis, report conclusion, quality review

controls.requirement: Assessment reports MUST receive factual review and independent quality review before issuance.
controls.evidence: Management responses, review notes, reviewer sign-off, issued report hash

controls.requirement: Active claims MUST follow an organization-approved surveillance interval derived from impact, change rate, control frequency, incident history, applicable obligations, and claim period; I3 intervals must be shorter than otherwise comparable lower-impact intervals, and material change, major incident, invalid evidence, or withdrawal of relied-upon supplier assurance triggers immediate review.
controls.evidence: Approved cadence policy and system-specific rationale, legal/contractual mapping, claim-period record, I3 escalation comparison, surveillance reports, change/incident and supplier triggers

controls.requirement: Corrective actions MUST identify root cause, owner, due date, remediation, validation method, and closure evidence.
controls.evidence: Corrective-action record, validation results, assessor closure

profiles.name: Assistant
profiles.inclusionTest: Generates content or advice without executing external side effects

profiles.name: RAG
profiles.inclusionTest: Uses retrieved sources at inference time
profiles.primaryRisk: poisoned, unauthorized, stale, or ungrounded context

profiles.name: Coding agent
profiles.inclusionTest: Reads, writes, reviews, or executes software artifacts
profiles.primaryRisk: vulnerable code, secret exposure, destructive execution

profiles.name: Transactional agent
profiles.inclusionTest: Initiates or changes external records, payments, messages, permissions, or physical state

profiles.name: Multi-agent
profiles.inclusionTest: Delegates among two or more model-driven agents
profiles.primaryRisk: authority propagation, coordination failure, opaque provenance

profiles.name: High-impact
profiles.inclusionTest: Meets I3 or a legal/policy high-impact designation
profiles.primaryRisk: harm to rights, safety, essential access, or livelihood

autonomyLevels.definition: No action; output is not used for a consequential decision
Recommends; a human independently decides and executes
Executes reversible, bounded actions with pre-authorization
autonomyLevels.governancePosture: least privilege, action logs, tested rollback

autonomyLevels.definition: Executes consequential or externally visible actions without per-action approval
autonomyLevels.governancePosture: independent assurance, runtime policy enforcement, emergency stop

autonomyLevels.definition: Pursues open-ended goals or can alter its own authority, tools, or safeguards
autonomyLevels.governancePosture: prohibited unless an approved high-impact governance program explicitly authorizes a bounded deployment

impactLevels.definition: Negligible; no credible harm beyond inconvenience
impactLevels.examples: internal drafting with no sensitive data
low-value support error, reversible workflow delay

impactLevels.definition: Material financial, security, privacy, operational, or reputational harm
impactLevels.examples: production code change, customer transaction, sensitive-data disclosure

impactLevels.definition: Severe or systemic harm to safety, rights, livelihood, essential services, or many affected persons
impactLevels.examples: employment, credit, healthcare, critical infrastructure, biometric categorization

evidenceAttributes.acceptanceTest: Source identity and integrity can be verified.
Responsible person, service, or process is identifiable.
System, environment, component, control, and period are explicit.
Evidence falls within the assessment period or proves current design.
Relevant failures, exclusions, and populations are included.
A competent reviewer can repeat the test or trace the result.
Access, integrity, retention, and lawful handling are enforced.

evidenceClasses.name: Design
evidenceClasses.examples: approved policy, threat model, architecture, test plan

evidenceClasses.name: Operation
evidenceClasses.examples: logs, tickets, CI runs, alerts, sampled transactions

evidenceClasses.name: Outcome
evidenceClasses.examples: evaluation trend, incident rate, appeal outcome

soaDispositions.meaning: Requirement not fully satisfied; active exception meets this document
Requirement not satisfied and no valid exception exists

crosswalks.title: EU AI Act Engineering Map
crosswalks.description: Give engineering teams an honest, evidence-oriented map from EU AI Act concepts to AIES artifacts — without claiming CE marking, notified-body approval, or legal classification.
frameworks: Indicative evidence map — not conformity / CE

crosswalks.title: ISO AI Management, Risk, and Impact Crosswalk
crosswalks.description: Map AIES evidence artifacts to the management-system, AI risk-management, and AI system impact-assessment concerns in ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, and ISO/IEC 42005.

crosswalks.title: NIST AI Risk Crosswalk
crosswalks.description: Map AIES artifacts to NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 functions and the NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile.

crosswalks.title: OWASP LLM and Agentic Security Crosswalk
crosswalks.description: Map AIES prevention, detection, and response artifacts to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 and OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026.

crosswalks.title: MCP, A2A, and GenAI Observability Crosswalk
crosswalks.description: Define how AIES contracts record security and telemetry evidence for Model Context Protocol authorization, Agent2Agent interoperability, and OpenTelemetry Generative AI semantic conventions.

crosswalks.title: Secure Software and AI Supply-Chain Crosswalk
crosswalks.description: Map AIES artifacts to NIST SSDF SP 800-218, applicable NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls, SLSA, and OpenSSF practices.
